<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Śṛṅgāramañjarī&quot; by Ajitasena is a classic of Sanskrit literature that explores the theme of love and desire. The work consists of 128 ślokas or verses, each of which is composed of two lines in the Anuṣṭup meter.<br>The poem is divided into seven chapters, each of which focuses on a different aspect of love. The first chapter describes the different stages of courtship, from the initial attraction between the lovers to their eventual union.<br>The second chapter explores the various emotions that arise in a love relationship, such as joy, longing, and jealousy. The third chapter focuses on the physical beauty of the lovers, describing their various body parts and comparing them to natural objects like flowers and trees.<br>The fourth chapter delves deeper into the emotions of the lovers, exploring their feelings of separation and reunion. The fifth chapter describes the different kinds of love, including playful love, compassionate love, and intense love.<br>The sixth chapter is dedicated to the power of love, describing how it can overcome even the most difficult obstacles. The final chapter brings the work to a close with a meditation on the ultimate union of the lovers, both in this life and in the afterlife.<br>Overall, &quot;Śṛṅgāramañjarī&quot; is a beautiful and lyrical exploration of the joys and sorrows of love, and it continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars and lovers of Sanskrit literature.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Śṛṅgāramañjarī&quot; by Ajitasena consists of seven chapters or sections, each of which explores a different aspect of love and desire. The contents of each chapter are as follows:<br>Chapter 1: Madya-vibhrama (Intoxication)<br>This chapter describes the different stages of courtship, from the initial attraction between the lovers to their eventual union.<br>Chapter 2: Khaṇḍita-viḷāsa (Playful Anger)<br>This chapter explores the various emotions that arise in a love relationship, such as joy, longing, and jealousy.<br>Chapter 3: Unmadoddhāta (Intoxicated by Love)<br>This chapter focuses on the physical beauty of the lovers, describing their various body parts and comparing them to natural objects like flowers and trees.<br>Chapter 4: Viyōginī (Separated Lover)<br>This chapter delves deeper into the emotions of the lovers, exploring their feelings of separation and reunion.<br>Chapter 5: Khaṇḍita-bhāva (Angry Feelings)<br>This chapter describes the different kinds of love, including playful love, compassionate love, and intense love.<br>Chapter 6: Prośītabhartṛkā (Yearning for the Absent Lover)<br>This chapter is dedicated to the power of love, describing how it can overcome even the most difficult obstacles.<br>Chapter 7: Svādhīna-bhartṛkā (Submission to the Beloved)<br>The final chapter brings the work to a close with a meditation on the ultimate union of the lovers, both in this life and in the afterlife.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Śṛṅgāramañjarī&quot; by Ajitasena is a unique work of Sanskrit literature for several reasons. Firstly, it is a comprehensive exploration of the theme of love and desire, delving into the many different emotions and experiences that arise in a romantic relationship. Secondly, it is written in a style that is both lyrical and accessible, using vivid imagery and metaphors to capture the beauty and complexity of love. Finally, it is notable for its use of the Anuṣṭup meter, a common meter in Sanskrit poetry that is both rhythmic and elegant, giving the work a pleasing and memorable quality. Overall, &quot;Śṛṅgāramañjarī&quot; remains an important contribution to the tradition of Sanskrit literature, and continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars and lovers of poetry around the world.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Śṛṅgāramañjarī is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature for several reasons. Firstly, it is a masterful example of the Kāvya genre of poetry, which is known for its use of intricate wordplay, metaphor, and imagery. Secondly, the work offers a comprehensive exploration of the theme of love and desire, providing a rich source of inspiration for subsequent poets and writers. Thirdly, it exemplifies the sophisticated literary culture of ancient India, and demonstrates the deep insights and philosophical understanding that were a hallmark of Sanskrit literature.<br><br>Śṛṅgāramañjarī is considered one of the finest examples of Sanskrit literature on the subject of love and desire. The work is notable for its vivid descriptions of various moods and emotions associated with love, such as longing, desire, jealousy, and heartbreak. It also features a wide range of characters, including kings, queens, courtesans, and commoners, all of whom are depicted with remarkable depth and sensitivity.</div></div></div>
